La cara de esa muchacha es increíblemente fea.

delea1/la leche.why: Found by a second sweep of what an example SAYS: its middle sentence was 'Es hora de irse cagando leches de aquí', where cagando leches is coarse Spanish slang, on an A1 card about milk. It was the only hit in the whole deck when the English translations were swept the same way. Its Forms row also gave 'las leches', a plural leche does not usefully have — the los dineros fault again.
dropEx: Es hora de irse cagando leches de aquí.

delea1/poder.why: Right as far as it goes, and silent on the two things beside it: poder for PERMISSION (¿puedo pasar?), which is a different question from ability and the one an A1 reader asks first, and el poder, the masculine noun.

delea1/encontrar.why: 'to meet, to find, encounter, come across' puts the wrong sense first - encontrar is to FIND - and two of the four are bare infinitives with the 'to' dropped. What it left out is the reflexive, which is what BOTH of the card's last two examples are: encontrarse con somebody, to run into them, and encontrarse, to feel.
senses: encontrarse con — to meet, to run into

delea1/cinco.why: Its second example is 'Me gustaría tres veintes, seis cincos, y el resto en unos' - changing money into American banknote denominations, which is neither A1 nor about the number. las cinco, telling the time, is how a reader meets the word.
dropEx: Me gustaría tres veintes, seis cincos, y el resto en unos.

delea1/el niño, la niña.why: The only pair card in the deck that already glossed both halves, and it did so as a flat list - 'child, boy, girl' - rather than saying which word is which. Brought into the shape the other four now have, with the masculine plural named.

delea1/la cara.why: Two dictionary definitions of the same word - 'face (the front part of the head)' and 'face (one's facial expression)'. The side of a coin or a page, and cara a cara, are what the second bullet could usefully have been.
senses: side, face (of a coin or a sheet)
cara a cara — face to face

delea1/cerca.why: Six glosses in one line - 'close, near, around, about, nearly, nigh' - the last of which is archaic English. cerca DE, which is what the card's own first example is, had no line; nor did la cerca, the feminine noun meaning a fence, which is what its second example bolds.
senses: cerca de — near, close to; about, nearly (cerca de cien)

delea1/viejo, vieja.why: Two disambiguated glosses both meaning old. What a reader needs beside them is that viejo of a PERSON is blunt and mayor is the polite word - which the deck teaches nowhere, though mayor is already in bien's and grande's orbit.
senses: old (of a person; mayor is politer)

delea1/bastante.why: Filed as an ADJECTIVE, and TWO of its three examples are the adverb - bastante atractiva, bastante calor, meaning quite or fairly. Sixth card in this review whose part of speech and examples disagree, after hasta, mañana, demasiado, cuál and cuánto.
senses: quite, fairly, rather (bastante caro — quite expensive)
enough, quite a lot of (bastantes personas)

delea1/el fin.why: 'end' and then four words for purpose. ALL THREE of its examples are phrases the card did not list: al fin y al cabo, and el fin de semana twice - the weekend, which is the shape an A1 reader meets this word in far more often than as an end.
senses: el fin de semana — the weekend
al fin y al cabo — after all
a fin de — in order to

delea1/tomar.why: 'to take, to select, choose' - and not to HAVE or to DRINK, which is what tomar does in a café and is the first thing a reader will need it for (tomar un café, ¿qué vas a tomar?). Catching a bus is the other everyday sense and was also missing.
senses: to have, to drink (tomar un café — to have a coffee)

delea1/el punto.why: Two dictionary definitions, and neither of the two things a beginner needs: el punto is the full stop, and en punto is how Spanish tells the time on the hour. Its third example bolds puntito, a diminutive rather than a form of the word.
senses: en punto — on the dot (las tres en punto — three o'clock sharp)
el punto de vista — the point of view
dropEx: Nuestra Vía Láctea solo es un puntito insignificante en el universo.

delea1/cuándo.why: Right, and the card could not say the one thing that most needs saying about it: cuando without the accent is a different word, the conjunction, which had no card in this deck at all until this batch added one.

delea1/grande.why: 'big, large, great, grand' with nothing to tell them apart - and what tells them apart is POSITION: un hombre grande is a big man and un gran hombre a great one. gran, the form it takes before a singular noun, is the fourth apocopation in this deck after buen, mal and primer, and like them had no card and no mention. mayor, which the card's own third example bolds, was not there either.
senses: great (before the noun: un gran hombre)

delea1/llegar.why: Four glosses, two of them bare infinitives with the 'to' dropped, all of them 'to arrive'. llegar tarde, which is what the card's own first example is, and llegar a ser had no line.
senses: to arrive, to get (to a place)
to reach, to get up to

delea1/el coche.why: 'carriage, coach, car' puts the horse-drawn senses first and the one a reader needs third. coche is also Peninsular; much of Latin America says carro or auto, which the deck says nowhere.

delea1/la clase.why: 'lecture' first, which is not what any of the card's three examples mean, and no sense for clase as a KIND - ¿qué clase de…? - which is the other half of the word.

delea1/cuatro.why: Two of its three examples are telling the time, which the card did not name - the same line tres and cinco now carry.

delea1/pequeño, pequeña.why: 'small, little' and no comparative: menor, which is the word for a younger brother or sister and is what the card's own third example is really about (mi hermana pequeña). The mirror of grande and mayor.
senses: young, younger (mi hermano pequeño — my little brother)

delea1/allá.why: 'there, over there, thither, yonder' - two of those are archaic English - and ALL THREE of the card's examples are más allá de, meaning beyond, which it did not list. It also never said where allá stands among aquí, ahí and allí, which the other three now all do.
senses: over there (vaguer and further than allí)

delea1/la tierra.why: 'Earth, land, ground' with no mark on which is which: la Tierra capitalised is the planet, and lower-case tierra is land, soil or the ground. The card's own first example is the soil.

delea1/final.why: FOUND BY A PROBE FOR A GLOSS WITH UNBALANCED BRACKETS. The extractor splits a dictionary's sense list on the comma, and a comma INSIDE a parenthesis splits it too - so one gloss arrives as two fragments, neither of which is a translation. tampoco was the first found (batch 5) and there are five more; every one is fixed here. This card's four glosses were 'final (last', 'ultimate)', 'final (conclusive' and 'decisive)'. It is also a NOUN - el final is the end, which is what the card's own first example is (al final) - and la final is a sporting final.
senses: el final — the end (al final — in the end)

delea1/la película.why: FOUND BY A PROBE FOR A GLOSS WITH UNBALANCED BRACKETS. The extractor splits a dictionary's sense list on the comma, and a comma INSIDE a parenthesis splits it too - so one gloss arrives as two fragments, neither of which is a translation. tampoco was the first found (batch 5) and there are five more; every one is fixed here. Its glosses were 'film (layer)', 'movie (US', 'Canada)' and 'film' - the everyday sense split in half and then repeated.
senses: film, thin layer (una película de polvo)

delea1/la izquierda.why: FOUND BY A PROBE FOR A GLOSS WITH UNBALANCED BRACKETS. The extractor splits a dictionary's sense list on the comma, and a comma INSIDE a parenthesis splits it too - so one gloss arrives as two fragments, neither of which is a translation. tampoco was the first found (batch 5) and there are five more; every one is fixed here. Its glosses were 'left (side', 'direction)' and 'left'. a la izquierda, which is how the word is used, had no line, and neither did the political sense. Its second example is the ADJECTIVE izquierda (el ala izquierda), which the card did not list either.
senses: izquierdo, izquierda — left (el ala izquierda — the left wing)
a la izquierda — on the left, to the left

delea1/la tarjeta.why: FOUND BY A PROBE FOR A GLOSS WITH UNBALANCED BRACKETS. The extractor splits a dictionary's sense list on the comma, and a comma INSIDE a parenthesis splits it too - so one gloss arrives as two fragments, neither of which is a translation. tampoco was the first found (batch 5) and there are five more; every one is fixed here. This one had NO usable gloss at all: its two fragments were 'card (only sometimes' and 'see carta)' — a lexicographer's cross-reference, split in half, standing where the translation should be. The distinction it was pointing at is worth stating properly, since carta has a card of its own. Note when replacing a Forms block: the plural has to be carried across with it, or the card's own example goes unmarked — tarjetas did, for one run.
senses: card (a bank card, a postcard, a business card)
la tarjeta de crédito — credit card
forms: a letter or a menu is

delea1/abierto, abierta.why: FOUND BY A PROBE FOR A GLOSS WITH UNBALANCED BRACKETS. The extractor splits a dictionary's sense list on the comma, and a comma INSIDE a parenthesis splits it too - so one gloss arrives as two fragments, neither of which is a translation. tampoco was the first found (batch 5) and there are five more; every one is fixed here. Its glosses were 'open', 'unlocked (not closed', 'accessible)' and 'open (actively conducting business)'. It is also the past participle of abrir, which has its own card and was not named.

delea1/pensar.why: 'to think, ponder, to reflect, think through' - four glosses, two of them bare infinitives with the 'to' dropped. pensar EN, which is what the card's own first example is (pensar en Mary), and pensar + infinitive for an intention had no line.
senses: pensar + infinitive — to intend to (pienso ir)
¿qué piensas de…? — what do you think of…?

delea1/trabajar.why: 'to work, to work in, work on, to workshop (+ en)' - the last is not English for anything trabajar does. trabajar de or como, which is how you say what job somebody has, was missing.
senses: trabajar de, trabajar como — to work as (trabaja de camarero)
trabajar en — to work at, to work on

delea1/el juego.why: Its first and third examples are the SAME SENTENCE with a different name in it - 'A ella le gustan los juegos de palabras' and 'A Tom le gustan los juegos de palabras'. un juego de llaves, a set, was also not listed.
senses: set (un juego de llaves — a set of keys)
dropEx: A Tom le gustan los juegos de palabras.

delea1/el teléfono.why: Right, and thin: por teléfono is what the card's own first example is, and el teléfono móvil - el celular across most of Latin America - is what its third one is.
senses: el teléfono móvil — mobile phone (el celular in Latin America)

delea1/la fiesta.why: 'party, feast' - and the sense the card's own second example uses, a public holiday (antes de las fiestas), was not among them.
senses: public holiday, festival (las fiestas — the holidays)

delea1/dar.why: 'to give, to give out, to hand over' - three ways of saying one thing, and TWO of the card's three examples are idioms it did not list: dar las gracias, to thank, and dar miedo, to frighten. dar is the verb Spanish builds most of its everyday expressions on and the card said so nowhere.

delea1/vivir.why: Its first example is 'Como desearía poder volver a vivir mí vida', where mí carries an accent it should not have - mi is the determiner and mí the pronoun, a distinction the mi card now states. That is the fourth grammar mistake found in the deck's own Spanish. vivir en, which is what a reader will say first, had no line.
senses: vivir en — to live in (a place)
vivir de — to live on, to make a living from
dropEx: Como desearía poder volver a vivir mí vida.

delea1/posible.why: 'possible' alone; es posible que, which is the card's own first example, and lo antes posible are the two shapes the word is met in.
senses: es posible que — it's possible that, maybe
lo antes posible — as soon as possible

delea1/el número.why: 'number (counting)' and 'musical number', the second being a sense of the English word rather than a use a reader will meet. el número de teléfono is the card's own third example, and a shoe size is the other everyday sense.
senses: el número de teléfono — phone number

delea1/la escuela.why: 'school (an institution dedicated to teaching and learning)' is a definition rather than a translation. What a reader needs beside it is that el colegio and el instituto are the words they will meet as often, which the deck says nowhere.
senses: ir a la escuela — to go to school

delea1/la pregunta.why: A definition for a gloss, and no HACER UNA PREGUNTA - which is what the card's own second example is, and is the thing an English speaker gets wrong first, since Spanish does not say preguntar una pregunta.
senses: hacer una pregunta — to ask a question
contestar una pregunta — to answer a question

delea1/segundo, segunda.why: Glossed as the ordinal alone, while the card's own third example is 'doce segundos' - el segundo, the unit of time, which it did not list.

delea1/la comida.why: 'food, lunch' - and MEAL, which is what both of the card's first two examples are (después de la comida, después de las comidas), was not there. Which meal comida names also varies: in Spain it is the midday one.

delea1/fácil.why: 'easy, facile, simple' - facile is a false friend, meaning glib in English rather than easy. Its opposite has a card of its own and neither pointed at the other.
senses: es fácil de + infinitive — it is easy to (fácil de encontrar)

delea1/el vino.why: Right, and thin: tinto and blanco are the two words a reader needs the moment they order any.

delea1/la habitación.why: Two dictionary definitions of the same word. What is missing is the use a beginner needs it for first: a hotel room, una habitación doble.
senses: hotel room (una habitación doble — a double room)

delea1/creer.why: 'to believe' and then four more words for it. creer EN, which is what the card's own third example is, and creo que sí — which is how the whole word is most often heard — had no line.
senses: creo que sí — I think so; creo que no — I don't think so

delea1/joven.why: 'young, youthful' and no mention that joven is also a NOUN - el joven, a young man - or that its comparative is menor, which is what the card's own second example bolds.
senses: el joven, la joven — a young man, a young woman

delea1/esperar.why: 'to hope, to expect' - and TO WAIT, which is what BOTH of the card's first two examples are (vamos a esperar aquí, está esperando en la parada del autobús), was not among them. One verb, three English words, and the deck carried the two a reader needs least.
senses: espero que sí — I hope so
esperar a alguien — to wait for somebody

delea1/lejos.why: lejos DE, which is what two of the card's three examples are, had no line. Its first example is also poor Spanish - 'a unas cinco millas lejos de aquí' says the distance twice; a cinco millas de aquí is how it is said. Fifth grammar fault found in the deck's own sentences.
senses: a lo lejos — in the distance
dropEx: Está a unas cinco millas lejos de aquí.
ex: The airport is very far away.

delea1/alto, alta.why: 'tall, high' with nothing to say which goes with what - tall is for a person and high for a thing - and no en voz alta, which is how the word is met as often as either.
senses: loud (en voz alta — aloud, out loud)

delea1/seis.why: Two of its three examples are telling the time, which the card did not name - the line tres, cuatro and cinco now carry.

delea1/la oficina.why: Flagged by the junk-gloss sweep in batch 5 and left over from it. 'office (a room used for non-manual work)' is a definition, and 'workshop' is el taller rather than la oficina. The two compounds a reader will actually need are the post office and the tourist office.
senses: la oficina de correos — the post office
la oficina de turismo — the tourist office

delea1/la cama.why: 'bed' alone, while BOTH of the phrases the card's own examples use - irse a la cama and hacer la cama - had no line.
senses: irse a la cama — to go to bed
hacer la cama — to make the bed

delea1/dormir.why: 'to sleep, to fall asleep' - and to fall asleep is dormirse, the reflexive, which is a different form rather than a second meaning of the same one. dormir la siesta was missing.
senses: dormir la siesta — to have a nap

delea1/ayudar.why: 'to help' alone, and the card's own first example is ayudar A cuidar - the preposition before the infinitive, which is exactly what an English speaker leaves out.
senses: ayudar a + infinitive — to help (to) do something
¿en qué puedo ayudarle? — how can I help you?

delea1/el marido.why: Its third example is 'Mary le puso los cuernos a su marido' - poner los cuernos, a colloquial idiom about infidelity, which the card does not teach and an A1 reader does not need. The feminine has no card of its own, so the two words for a wife go in Forms.
dropEx: Mary le puso los cuernos a su marido.
ex: Su marido trabaja en un banco.
Her husband works in a bank.

delea1/el pueblo.why: 'town, village, the common people, the working classes' - the last two are one sense written twice, and it is a different sense from the first two, so they belong in blocks of their own rather than in one list.
senses: the people (of a country: el pueblo español)

delea1/la música.why: ALL THREE of its examples were the same sentence: 'A todo el mundo le gusta la música', the same again as a question, and the same with a different subject. That is the worst duplication in the deck after entre's three. 'song' is la canción, which has a card of its own; what música does carry besides the mass noun is a female musician. Its Forms row also gave las músicas, a plural the word does not usefully have.
dropEx: ¿A todo el mundo le gusta la música?
A mi padre no le gusta la música.
ex: I listen to music every day.

delea1/el minuto.why: A definition - 'a unit of time equal to 60 seconds or 1/60 hour' - and then the word itself as the second gloss.

delea1/llamarse.why: The gloss is right and the card never asks the question the word exists for: ¿cómo te llamas? is the first sentence in any Spanish course. llamar without the se - to call, to phone - has no card in the deck either, so it goes in Forms. It also showed up a gap in the tool: a reflexive verb's conjugation table carries its pronoun ('me llamo', 'te llamas'), so every cell is two words and the rebold dropped them all — all three of this card's examples came back with nothing marked. The pronoun is stripped now, which is what the generator's own bolding does.
senses: to be called (me llamo Ana — my name is Ana)
¿cómo se llama usted? — what is your name? (formal)

delea1/el país.why: 'country (the territory of a nation)', then 'country', then 'land' - a definition followed by the word itself. What is worth a line instead is that the English 'country' meaning countryside is el campo, which has its own card and is the confusion an English speaker actually has.

delea1/el rey, la reina.why: A pair card that already glosses both halves — and the masculine plural means the king AND queen together, and los Reyes Magos are who bring Spanish children their presents on 6 January. Neither was there.
senses: los reyes — the king and queen; los Reyes Magos — the Three Wise Men

delea1/diez.why: Two of its three examples are diez minutos and one is telling the time, which the card did not name.

delea1/el hospital.why: 'hospital' alone. estar en el hospital, which is the card's own second example, is worth the line because Spanish keeps the article where English drops it.
senses: estar en el hospital — to be in hospital

delea1/llevar.why: 'to take somewhere, to carry, bear, hold' - four glosses for one sense, and neither of the two things llevar does that an A1 reader needs most: TO WEAR (llevar una camisa) and llevar + a length of time (llevo dos años aquí), which is how Spanish says how long something has been going on. llevarse was missing too.
senses: to take, to carry (to a place)
to have been (llevo dos años aquí — I've been here two years)
llevarse — to take away; llevarse bien con — to get on well with

delea1/poner.why: 'to put, to write' - and PONERSE, which is what the card's own third example is (el cielo se puso oscuro), was not there. It is two things at once, putting clothes on and becoming, and both are A1. poner la mesa goes with it. Its second example bolds póngase, an imperative with the pronoun attached, which no person-and-number table has a row for — the same shape as hay on the haber card, and named the same way.
senses: ponerse — to put on (clothes); to become (se puso rojo — he went red)
poner la mesa — to lay the table

delea1/la calle.why: 'street' and then a definition of a swimming lane that specifies what it is not. en la calle, which is how the word is used, is the better second line.
senses: en la calle — in the street, outside

delea1/el café.why: 'coffee, cafe, coffee shop' - the last two are one thing. What the card needed instead is how coffee is ordered, which is its own second example: con leche and solo.
senses: el café con leche — white coffee

delea1/empezar.why: 'to start, begin, to get started' - three ways of saying one thing, one of them with the 'to' dropped - and not empezar A, the preposition before an infinitive, which is what an English speaker leaves out.
senses: empezar a + infinitive — to start doing something

delea1/cuarto, cuarta.why: Glossed 'fourth' alone, and TWO of its three examples are the masculine NOUN el cuarto meaning a room - compañero de cuarto, cinco cuartos - which the card did not list. The other thing cuarto does is a quarter, which is how Spanish tells the time at quarter past.

delea1/buscar.why: Five glosses on one line - 'to seek, search for, look for, try to find, to scour'. What is worth saying instead is that buscar takes NO preposition: se busca algo, never se busca POR algo, which is the mistake an English speaker makes with this verb every time. ir a buscar, which is the card's own first example, had no line.
senses: to look for, to search for
ir a buscar — to go and fetch, to pick up

delea1/jugar.why: 'to play, to risk, take a chance' - and not jugar A, which is what ALL THREE of the card's examples have (jugar al tenis, jugar a las cartas). Spanish also plays an instrument with a different verb, tocar, which is the confusion that follows immediately and which the deck did not mention.
senses: to play (a game or a sport)
jugar a — to play (jugar al fútbol, jugar a las cartas)

delea1/el presidente, la presidenta.why: 'president, head (leader)' — the second a description. The chair of a meeting or a company is the sense a reader will meet as often, and it is the same word.
senses: chairman, chairwoman (of a company or a meeting)

delea1/la información.why: 'data' is los datos rather than información. The plural informaciones, which the card's own second example uses, is real but means separate items of news; the desk you ask at is worth more to a beginner.
senses: la oficina de información — the information desk

delea1/usar.why: 'to use, to wear' is right, and it needs the regional note the llevar card now forces: Spain says llevar for wearing clothes and much of Latin America says usar, so a reader meeting both wants to know they are the same thing.
senses: to wear (chiefly Latin America; Spain says llevar)

delea1/ayer.why: 'yesterday' alone, while both of the card's first two examples are ayer por la noche and ayer por la tarde, and anteayer has no card anywhere in the deck.
senses: ayer por la mañana — yesterday morning

delea1/el negro.why: THE ONLY COLOUR IN THE DECK HEADED AS A NOUN. blanco, rojo, verde and azul are all adjectives; this one was 'el negro', glossed 'black (the color perceived in the absence of light)', while two of its three examples are the adjective (negra, negros). Headed as a masculine noun, el negro also names a person, which is a different and loaded word — and the card's second example is 'El sospechoso es un varón de raza negra', a police description of a suspect, on an A1 card about a colour. It is the adjective now, like its four siblings, with the colour noun as a second sense.
dropEx: El sospechoso es un varón de raza negra.

delea1/blanco, blanca.why: The other half of the negro entry: its second gloss was 'white (of light skin)', a racial sense given equal billing with the colour on an A1 card. What blanco does need is en blanco, and el vino blanco, which the vino card now carries from the other side.
senses: el blanco — the colour white; a target

delea1/el mensaje.why: 'message, speech' - speech is el discurso. el mensaje de texto, which is the card's own second example, is what the second line should have been.
senses: el mensaje de texto — text message
dejar un mensaje — to leave a message

delea1/cambiar.why: Five glosses for one verb, and its second example is not a verb at all - 'el tipo de cambio' is the masculine NOUN el cambio, the exchange rate, which the card did not list. cambiar DE, which is what its third example is (cambié de tren), had no line either.
senses: cambiar de — to change (cambiar de tren, cambiar de idea)
el cambio — change; the exchange rate

delea1/el médico, la médica.why: 'doctor, physician' - one word twice. ir al médico is the phrase a reader needs and it was not there.
senses: ir al médico — to go to the doctor

delea1/largo, larga.why: Its second gloss was five synonyms of its first - 'long, lengthy, extended, prolonged, protracted'. What the card most needed to say is that largo is a FALSE FRIEND: English 'large' is grande, and this is the mistake an English speaker makes with it before any other. a lo largo de, which is the card's own first example, had no line.
senses: a lo largo de — along, throughout

delea1/el baño.why: 'bath (act of taking a bath)' first, which is not what any of the three examples mean - all three are the room. el cuarto de baño and ir al baño are how a reader will use the word.
senses: bath (tomar un baño — to have a bath)
el cuarto de baño — the bathroom
ir al baño — to go to the toilet

delea1/la edad.why: 'time since an event' is a definition rather than a translation. ¿qué edad tienes? is how the word is used and la Edad Media is where a reader will next meet it.
senses: ¿qué edad tienes? — how old are you?
la Edad Media — the Middle Ages

delea1/el aire.why: Two dictionary definitions of the same word. al aire libre and el aire acondicionado are the two compounds a beginner meets.
senses: al aire libre — outdoors, in the open air

delea1/tuyo.why: The mirror of mío, and it had the same three faults: two examples where every other card has three, no Forms though its second example bolds tuyas, and only the pronoun - un amigo tuyo, the stressed possessive after its noun, was not there.
senses: of yours, your own (after the noun: un amigo tuyo)
ex: A friend of yours called me.

delea1/el campo.why: 'countryside, country, field (large open area)' - and the card's own third example is a campo de golf, a course, which is the sporting sense it did not list.
senses: el campo de fútbol — football pitch; el campo de golf — golf course

delea1/la foto.why: Right, and silent on the trap: foto is FEMININE although it ends in -o, because it is short for la fotografía. The deck states the mirror of that on el día and said nothing here. hacer una foto, which is the card's own first example, had no line.
senses: hacer una foto, sacar una foto — to take a photo

delea1/el abogado, la abogada.why: Three synonyms, the last of them carrying a stray full stop out of the dictionary: 'lawyer, solicitor, counsel.'

delea1/pagar.why: 'to be worthwhile' and 'to have a pay off' are one idiomatic sense written twice, from the proverb the card's own third example is. What a reader needs instead is how to pay: en efectivo or con tarjeta.
senses: to pay for (pagar la cuenta — to pay the bill)
pagar en efectivo — to pay cash
pagar con tarjeta — to pay by card

delea1/el pelo.why: Two dictionary definitions telling one hair from a head of hair, which a reader will never need told. cortarse el pelo is the phrase they will need, and por los pelos is the card's own second example.
senses: cortarse el pelo — to have one's hair cut
por los pelos — by the skin of one's teeth

delea1/la cena.why: Right, and the verb it is built on has a card of its own with neither pointing at the other.

delea1/sentir.why: Its third example bolds SENTIDO in 'no tiene ningún sentido' - the masculine noun meaning sense or meaning, not a form of this verb. And the two things sentir is most used for were both missing: sentirse plus an adjective (me siento mal, which the mal card now shows), and LO SIENTO, which is the first apology a reader will ever make in Spanish.
senses: to feel (sentir dolor — to feel pain)
sentirse — to feel (me siento bien — I feel well)
dropEx: Una vida sin amor no tiene ningún sentido.

delea1/bonito, bonita.why: Nine glosses - 'pretty, cute, nice, lovely, sweet, fine, charming, great' - for a word that means pretty.

delea1/la tienda.why: 'tent' first, and not one of the card's three examples is a tent - all three are a shop. The tent is la tienda de campaña, which is worth its own line rather than the head of the list.

delea1/la mesa.why: Its second gloss was 'mesa' — the Spanish word glossed with the English loanword of itself, which is the geological flat-topped hill and tells a reader nothing. Its own second example translates mesas as 'desks', a sense it did not list, and poner la mesa is what the poner card now carries from the other side.
senses: poner la mesa — to lay the table

delea1/la carta.why: 'letter (document), map' — and the two senses an A1 reader meets first were both absent: the MENU in a restaurant, and PLAYING CARDS, which is what the card's own second example is (jugamos a las cartas). The tarjeta card now points here for the distinction, and this is the other half of it.

delea1/el novio, la novia.why: 'boyfriend (romantic partner), fiancé', so GIRLFRIEND was missing from a pair card - the fifth in this deck after el hijo la hija, el hermano la hermana, el chico la chica and el tío la tía. novia is also the bride, and los novios the couple getting married, neither of which was there. Its third example also spelt éste with the accent the RAE dropped in 2010, and said nothing the first two did not; it makes room for the wedding sense.
senses: los novios — the couple; the bride and groom
dropEx: Ella tiene muchos novios, pero éste es especial.
ex: Los novios salieron de la iglesia.
The bride and groom came out of the church.

delea1/comprar.why: 'to buy (to obtain in exchange of money or goods)' is a definition, and its English is wrong as well — in exchange FOR. 'to buy out' is a business sense no A1 reader needs. ir de compras, which is what the card's own first example is, had no line.
senses: ir de compras — to go shopping
comprar algo a alguien — to buy something for, or from, somebody

delea1/el centro.why: 'center' and then 'center, moderate tendencies or ideas' — the political sense given as much room as the ordinary one, and el centro comercial, which is where a reader will hear the word most, missing altogether.
senses: town centre, downtown (el centro de la ciudad)

delea1/el mes.why: 'month' alone, while both of the card's own examples are el mes pasado — the same line el año now carries.
senses: el mes que viene — next month

delea1/el sol.why: hace sol was missing, which is the weather phrase that goes with hace frío and hace calor on the hacer card, and so was tomar el sol. Its second example — 'como si se hubieran levantado siete soles dentro de mí' — is a poetic sentence in the subjunctive, well above this level.
dropEx: Me sentí como si se hubieran levantado siete soles dentro de mí.

delea1/la dirección.why: 'direction, address' in that order, though two of the card's three examples are the address. The management of a company is the third sense and was not there. Its first and third examples were also the same sentence with one verb changed.
dropEx: Tom no pudo averiguar la dirección de Mary.

delea1/siete.why: Two of its three examples are telling the time, which the card did not name — the line tres, cuatro, cinco, seis and diez now carry.

delea1/el barco.why: 'boat (usually with a concave hull)' is a definition, and a qualifier that distinguishes nothing a reader needs distinguished — all three of the card's examples translate it 'ship'. en barco was missing.
senses: en barco — by boat, by sea

delea1/acá.why: A COMPLETE MISS, like la cuenta's: the card was glossed 'as of' and 'up to', and acá means neither. It means HERE - the Latin American everyday word where Spain says aquí - which is exactly what all three of its own examples say (estoy acá, no estará acá, lo que pasó acá). Two glosses, neither of them the word, and three sentences all showing the sense it did not carry.
senses: here (chiefly Latin America; Spain says aquí)

delea1/el profesor, la profesora.why: 'professor (a faculty member)' first, which at A1 is the wrong way round - profesor is the schoolteacher a reader will meet, and the card's own second example is 'nuestra profesora de inglés'.

delea1/la canción.why: Its first example is clumsy Spanish - '¿Cuál es tu letra de una canción favorita?' for 'what's your favourite song lyric' - and its third asks the same question again about Bob Dylan. The verb it goes with has a card and neither pointed at the other. The verb cross-reference in Forms then made cantar a bold target and the first example marked it, which is why the tool now reports an example whose only bolded word is another card's headword.
dropEx: ¿Cuál es tu letra de una canción favorita?

delea1/la universidad.why: Its third example is MISTRANSLATED: 'Ese hombre es definitivamente un estudiante de universidad' is rendered 'That man is definitely a bachelor', which is the other sense of the English word bachelor and not what the Spanish says at all. A reader learning from the pair would take estudiante de universidad to mean an unmarried man.
senses: ir a la universidad — to go to university
dropEx: Ese hombre es definitivamente un estudiante de universidad.

delea1/la sala.why: 'room (a separate part of a building)' is a definition and is also what la habitación and el cuarto are glossed with, so three cards said the same thing and none said what tells them apart: sala is the large or public room, and the living room. Its own second example is a sala de cine.
senses: room, hall (a large or public one)
la sala de espera — waiting room

delea1/escuchar.why: 'to listen to, to hear out, to hear' - and oír, which has a card of its own glossed 'to hear', is the verb for hearing without trying. The deck taught both and said nothing about the difference, which is the same shape as ser and estar or saber and conocer.

delea1/oír.why: The other half of the escuchar entry: 'to hear' and then 'to hear (passively perceive a sound)', the same gloss twice with a definition on the second.
senses: oír hablar de — to hear about

delea1/terminar.why: Four glosses on one line, and not terminar DE before an infinitive, which is how you say you have finished doing something.
senses: terminar de + infinitive — to finish doing something

delea1/ocho.why: 'eight (8)' repeats itself in brackets. Its first and third examples are the same sentence with escuela swapped for colegio, and its second is 'Sus ochos parecían ges minúsculas' - the plural of the written digit, which is the cincos fault again.
dropEx: Sus ochos parecían ges minúsculas.
El colegio empieza a las ocho y media.

delea1/el avión.why: 'aeroplane, airplane, plane' is one word written three ways, two of them the same word in two spellings. en avión was missing.

delea1/el abuelo, la abuela.why: Its second gloss was 'loose tufts of hair in the nape when one's hair is messed up' - a regional sense of abuelo lifted whole out of a dictionary and offered as the second thing to know about the word. GRANDMOTHER, meanwhile, was missing, on a card that is a pair: the sixth in this deck after el hijo, el hermano, el chico, el tío and el novio. los abuelos, which is the card's own third example, is grandparents.

delea1/la cocina.why: 'kitchen, stove, cooker, range' - three words for the appliance and none for COOKING, which is what the card's own third example is ('la cocina no es una de sus habilidades'). Its second example bolds cocinas in 'luego la cocinas' - the VERB cocinar in the second person, not the plural of the noun - and is a proverb about catching a hare.
senses: cooking, cuisine (la cocina española — Spanish cooking)
dropEx: Primero atrapa tu liebre y luego la cocinas.

delea1/la derecha.why: Its second example bolds derechas in 'las paredes no estaban derechas' - the ADJECTIVE derecho meaning straight, which is a different word from the noun the card teaches and which it did not list. a la derecha, which is its third example, had no line, and the political sense - which la izquierda now carries - was missing from this side.
senses: a la derecha — on the right, to the right

delea1/el piso.why: Two glosses about floors and neither of them the sense a reader in Spain meets first: EL PISO IS A FLAT. All three of the card's examples are the storey sense, so the commonest meaning of the word was nowhere on it.

delea1/el director, la directora.why: 'director, conductor (of a musical ensemble)' - and TWO of the card's three examples translate it 'principal', a head teacher, which it did not list.

delea1/el tren.why: 'train' alone, while the card's own third example is coger el tren - and which verb you use depends on where you are, coger in Spain and tomar across most of Latin America, where coger is obscene.
senses: coger el tren — to catch the train (tomar in Latin America)

delea1/el papel.why: 'paper, role' is right and bare; hacer el papel de is how the second sense is actually used.
senses: hacer el papel de — to play the part of

delea1/según.why: 'according to, as, just as, the same way' - four glosses across two parts of speech with nothing to separate them.
senses: as, depending on how (según te lo voy diciendo)

delea1/la iglesia.why: 'church' alone; ir a la iglesia is the card's own first example and Spanish drops the article where English keeps it the other way round.
senses: ir a la iglesia — to go to church

delea1/inteligente.why: Two examples where every other card has three - the fourth card in the deck short of one, after nadie, mío and tuyo.

delea1/beber.why: TWO of its three examples are about a BABY. 'El bebé se quedó dormido en la cuna' and 'Ella cogió a su bebe en sus brazos' bold bebé and bebe - the noun, matched because its letters are those of the third person of this verb. Two thirds of the card taught a word it does not teach, which is the worst instance of that fault found so far.
senses: beber algo — to have a drink
dropEx: El bebé se quedó dormido en la cuna.
Ella cogió a su bebe en sus brazos.
ex: What do you want to drink?

delea1/frío, fría.why: Its FIRST example is the masculine noun - 'azules del frío', blue with cold - which the card did not list. And neither hace frío nor tener frío was there, though the hacer and tener cards both now point at them from the other side.
senses: tener frío — to be cold (a person)

delea1/caliente.why: Its second example is ungrammatical: 'cosas que sean demasiadas calientes' - demasiado is an adverb here and does not agree. Seventh grammar fault found in the deck's own Spanish. The card also needed the distinction frío now carries from the other side: caliente describes a THING, and a person who feels hot says tengo calor - estar caliente of a person means something else entirely.
forms: a person who feels hot says
dropEx: No puedo comer o tomar cosas que sean demasiadas calientes.

delea1/mirar.why: Its second example bolds mirada - the feminine NOUN, a look or a glance - which is not a form of the verb. Its third is mirar hacia, to face, a sense the card did not list. ver has a card of its own and neither pointed at the other, though which of the two you use is a real question for a reader.
senses: mirar hacia — to face, to look out on
dropEx: Ella echó una mirada alrededor de la habitación.

delea1/entender.why: 'to understand, to fathom, to hear' - entender does not mean to hear, which is oír. no entiendo, which is the sentence a beginner needs most in a conversation, had no line.

delea1/hermoso, hermosa.why: Four glosses for one word, and its third example is 'Mi esposa no es hermosa. La suya sí' — my wife isn't beautiful, yours is — which is an unkind sentence to put in front of a beginner and teaches nothing the other two do not.
dropEx: Mi esposa no es hermosa. La suya sí.

delea1/el bar.why: 'bar, coffee shop, café, pub' - four words, and none of them says the thing a reader arriving in Spain needs to know: a bar there is one place that serves coffee in the morning and beer at night, and is where you have breakfast.
senses: bar, café (in Spain one place: coffee, drinks and food)

delea1/la carne.why: 'flesh' before 'an animal's meat', which is the wrong way round for a card a reader will meet in a shop, and the second is a definition rather than a translation.
senses: la carne de vaca — beef; la carne de cerdo — pork

delea1/la cerveza.why: 'beer' alone, and what a reader ordering one in Spain actually says is una caña, which the deck has nowhere.
senses: una caña — a small draught beer (Spain)

delea1/cenar.why: Glossed to dine / to have supper / to have a lavish meal - the third is a dictionary's marginal sense standing beside the everyday one, and none of the three says that cenar is transitive (cenamos pescado) or names la cena, which is the noun a reader meets on every menu and in every invitation. Its first two examples were also the same sentence twice, both eating out tonight.
senses: to have dinner, to have supper
to have (something) for dinner: cenamos pescado
la cena — dinner, the evening meal (late in Spain, from about nine)
dropEx: ¿Qué te parece si cenamos afuera esta noche?
ex: Tonight we are having fish for dinner.

delea1/el compañero, la compañera.why: Its fourth gloss was fellow X, classmate, coworker, etc. - a dictionary describing a pattern rather than translating the word, and the etc. leaves the reader to finish the job. What the word actually does is take a following de: de clase, de trabajo, de piso, and that is what the card should show.
senses: classmate, workmate, teammate — compañero de clase, de trabajo, de equipo
companion, someone you do something alongside

delea1/el norte.why: Its second gloss was north wind, a marginal sense given equal weight, while the three points of the compass that go with it - sur, este, oeste - were nowhere on the card. Two of its three examples were also the same sentence: my house is north of the city / of the library. Read again beside el sur: los nortes is not a plural anybody uses - a compass point has no plural - and the generator had carried it forward on both cards.
senses: al norte de — to the north of
el norte de España — the north of Spain
forms: el sur, el este, el oeste
dropEx: Mi casa queda al norte de la biblioteca.
ex: El tren sale hacia el norte a las ocho.
The train leaves for the north at eight.

delea1/el té.why: Its second example, Varios tés se venden aquí, is stilted where the card wants something a reader would say. The plural is still on the card in its Forms row.
dropEx: Varios tés se venden aquí.
ex: Would you like tea or coffee?

delea1/la ventana.why: Its second gloss was window frame, which is el marco, while the two windows a reader actually meets were missing: the one on a screen and la ventanilla, the small window of a car, a train or a ticket office.
forms: a car, train or ticket window

delea1/leer.why: One gloss, to read, and nothing about the two things this verb does that a reader will meet at once: leerse algo, which is reading a thing right through, and la lectura, the noun.
senses: leerse algo — to read something right through: me leí un libro

delea1/escribir.why: Its participle is irregular - escrito, not escribido - which is the one thing about this verb a reader has to remember, and the card never said so. It also had no room for ¿Cómo se escribe?, which is how you ask anybody in Spanish to spell something.
senses: to write to someone: le escribí a ella
escribirse — to be spelled: ¿cómo se escribe?

delea1/la estación.why: Both senses are listed and all three examples are the train station, so the season - which is the sense a reader is likelier to need first, and the one the four seasons hang off - is on the card in words and nowhere in use.
senses: station — la estación de tren, de autobuses, de metro
las cuatro estaciones — the four seasons: primavera, verano, otoño, invierno
dropEx: La estación de Tokio es la tercera parada.
ex: El otoño es mi estación favorita.

delea1/enfermo, enferma.why: Its third gloss was degenerate, a pejorative sense standing beside the everyday one - and meanwhile its own first example is the NOUN, el enfermo, the patient, which the card did not list at all. Nothing said estar enfermo or ponerse enfermo either, which is how the word is actually used.
senses: el enfermo, la enferma — the patient, the sick person

delea1/la salida.why: Three glosses and no sign of the verb it comes from, nor of the two compounds a reader meets on the first day: la salida de emergencia on every wall and la salida del sol.
senses: exit, way out — la salida de emergencia

delea1/bailar.why: Glossed to dance and to dribble (the ball) - the second a dictionary oddity given equal weight - while its own second example is el baile, the noun, which the card did not list, so one of the three sentences illustrated a word that was not on it.
senses: sacar a alguien a bailar — to ask someone to dance
dropEx: La pareja está en la pista de baile.
ex: Do you want to dance with me?

delea1/el sur.why: los sures is not a plural anybody uses - a compass point has no plural - and the card named none of the other three points, which is the one thing that makes this word worth a card of its own.
senses: al sur de — to the south of
el sur de España — the south of Spain
forms: el norte, el este, el oeste

delea1/aprender.why: One gloss, to learn, and no mention of aprender a + infinitive - which is what two of its own three examples do, and how the verb is used whenever what is learned is a skill rather than a subject.
senses: aprender a + infinitive — to learn to do something: aprender a nadar
aprender de memoria — to learn by heart

delea1/el precio.why: Glossed price, worth, cost - worth is el valor rather than a translation of this word - and it had none of the phrases a reader needs at a till.
senses: ¿qué precio tiene? — how much is it?
a buen precio — at a good price

delea1/el ojo.why: It shipped with two examples where every other card has three, and its second gloss was keyhole - which is el ojo de la cerradura, a compound rather than a sense of the bare word. Missing was ¡Ojo!, which is what a Spanish speaker actually says to make you watch out.
senses: el ojo de la cerradura — keyhole
ex: Tiene los ojos azules como su madre.
She has blue eyes like her mother.

delea1/azul.why: Correct as far as it went, and silent on the two things a colour card owes a reader: that azul is the same in the masculine and the feminine, and the everyday shades.
senses: blue (the same in the masculine and the feminine)
azul claro, azul oscuro — light blue, dark blue

delea1/el río.why: Its second example was carried by English that is not English - a large amount of rivers - which on the answer side of a card is the half a learner reads first.
dropEx: En Francia hay un gran número de ríos.
ex: El río pasa por el centro de la ciudad.
The river runs through the middle of the city.

delea1/abrir.why: Its participle is irregular - abierto, not abrido - and the card never said so, the same gap escribir had. Its three glosses were to open, open up and to unlock, of which the second is the first again and the third is not what abrir means on its own. Two of its three examples also opened the same window.
senses: abrirse — to open (of a door, a shop, a flower)
dropEx: Hacía calor, así es que abrí la ventana.
ex: What time do the shops open?

delea1/interior.why: Filed as an adjective and glossed inner, interior - and TWO of its own three examples are the noun: espacio en su interior, decoración de interiores. The third is la ropa interior, underwear, which is the compound a reader is likeliest to meet and which the card did not carry either.
senses: el interior — the inside, the interior

delea1/el apartamento.why: flat, apartment - and no word about the one thing that decides which of them a reader will hear: in Spain an ordinary flat is el piso, and apartamento is the smaller or the holiday sort.
senses: flat, apartment (in Spain usually a small one or a holiday let)

delea1/nueve.why: Right as far as it went, and every number card in the deck is worth its ordinal, which is the form a reader meets on a floor button and in a date.

delea1/traer.why: to bring, to bring about, cause, occasion - the last three are one marginal sense written out three ways - while the thing that actually makes this verb hard was missing: traer is bringing something HERE, and llevar is taking it away from here, a distinction English does not make with one pair of words.
senses: to bring — bringing something towards where the speaker is
llevar is its opposite: taking something away from here

delea1/suyo.why: his, hers, its, theirs - and not yours, which is what it means whenever the person is addressed as usted, and is the reason this word exists in a beginner deck at all. Nothing said it agrees with the thing owned rather than the owner, nor that it takes the article: el suyo, la suya.
senses: it agrees with the thing owned, not the owner: la suya, los suyos
with the article when it stands alone: el suyo es más grande
de él, de ella, de usted where suyo would be ambiguous

delea1/rojo, roja.why: Correct, and missing the two things a reader needs before the colour is any use: that going red is ponerse rojo, which its own second example does, and that red wine is not vino rojo but vino tinto.
senses: ponerse rojo — to blush, to go red
el vino tinto — red wine, never vino rojo

delea1/la entrada.why: entrance, entry, entering, admission, entryway - five near-synonyms for one sense - while the sense its own second example uses, the TICKET, was not listed at all: las entradas salen a la venta el lunes.
senses: ticket (for a cinema, a concert, a match)

delea1/la pareja.why: couple, pair, partner - and silent on the fact that trips up every learner: la pareja is feminine whoever it names, so a man is still mi pareja, and it is the ordinary word for the person you live with whether you are married or not.
senses: couple; the two of a pair
partner, the person you are with — feminine whoever it names: mi pareja es alto

delea1.why: THE DECK HAD NO THIRD-PERSON OBJECT PRONOUN AT ALL. supplement.py's PRONOUNS list names me, te, se, nos and os and stops, so DELE A1 shipped with cards for los and unas and nothing for lo, la, le or les - the pronouns an A1 reader needs the moment they stop using a noun twice in a sentence. The only trace of them was the los card's gloss, which called it 'a plural masculine or neuter pronoun' and gave no English at all; that card is now folded into the definite article, so without this the sense would have gone entirely. It also carries the neuter article lo, which turns an adjective into a noun (lo importante) and is a construction with no other home in the deck. The paradigm goes in Forms rather than in the headword, so the front of the card is not one letter away from the article's. Its Forms rows are the pronoun's own paradigm and not words to mark up, so the card names what may be bolded: deriving from them would bold the ARTICLE la in 'lo importante es la salud'.
senses: the … thing, what is … (neuter, before an adjective: lo importante)

delea1.why: The indirect object, missing for the same reason as lo. It carries the se rule in Forms - le and les become se before lo, la, los and las - which is the one thing about Spanish pronouns a reader cannot guess, and which the deck already shows in an example on the por card ('¿Por qué no se lo dijiste a ella?') without ever explaining. les is a form rather than a card, on the same reasoning that folded el, la, los and las into one.
senses: to him, to her, to you (formal) — indirect object
ex: Le di el libro a María.
I gave the book to María.

delea1.why: cómo had a card and como, one accent away and just as common, had none - so the deck taught the question word and not the ordinary conjunction that means 'as' or 'like'. It is also the one that turns up in a comparison (tan alto como) and in a reason clause (como llueve, no salgo), neither of which the deck could say anywhere. It is also the first person of comer, which is why the comer card's own examples bold it.
forms: with an accent, the question word
ex: Es tan alto como su padre.
He's as tall as his father.
Since it's raining, I'm not going out.

delea1.why: esto and eso each had a card and aquello, the third of the same set of three, had none - so the deck taught two thirds of a closed class and left the reader to guess the rest.
senses: that (neuter, further off — an idea, a situation, or something not yet named)
ex: I didn't like that at all.

delea1.why: The same gap as como, one accent over. supplement.py's QUESTION list names the ACCENTED interrogatives - qué, quién, cómo, cuándo, dónde, cuánto - and the deck therefore taught six question words and not one of the ordinary conjunctions written the same way without the accent. cuando is among the commonest words in Spanish and had no card. (donde is added beside it; quien and cual are deliberately left out — the relative quien is a B1 word and el cual is further on still, so adding them here would be teaching above the level rather than filling a gap.)
forms: with an accent, the question word
ex: I'll call you when I arrive.
Cuando era niño, vivía en Madrid.
When I was a child, I lived in Madrid.

delea1.why: See the cuando entry: the unaccented half of a question word the deck taught only as a question.
senses: where (as a relative: la casa donde vivo — the house where I live)
forms: with an accent, the question word
ex: Esta es la casa donde vivo.
This is the house where I live.
El pueblo donde nació es muy pequeño.
The village where he was born is very small.
